res.summary:
VERIFIED PAYMENT ARCHITECTURE FOR THE POOL PROTOTYPE (checked 2026-09-29)

INDIA (INR, UPI, cards, EMI): use Razorpay in test mode.
- Test mode opens right after signup. No KYC is needed.
- Flow: Orders API with transfers[] to the dealer's Route Linked Account, created with on_hold=true.
- When the buyer confirms the delivery or pickup code, call PATCH /v1/transfers/:id with on_hold=false to release the dealer payout. POOL's commission is whatever it does not transfer.
- Wave Drop rebate: pay it at pool close as a partial refund (POST refund with an amount, speed=optimum), plus reverse_all or a transfer reversal.
- Suggested design (not a vendor feature): split each order into two transfers, (a) the base payout, released on the delivery code, and (b) a "rebate reserve" transfer kept on hold until pool close. Then the Wave Drop refund never has to claw money back from a dealer.

HARD REGULATORY GATE (RBI PA Master Direction, 15 Sep 2025, read from the PDF text):
- Para 10: a PA may not run a marketplace business.
- Para 13(f): a marketplace may accept payments only for sellers onboarded on its platform.
- Escrow permitted-debit (iv): paying a third party (the dealer) on the merchant's instruction is allowed only if the merchant (POOL) has annual turnover above Rs 40 lakh (or export turnover above Rs 5 lakh), and the payee deals directly with the payer.
- Para 18(b): the escrow account cannot be used for Cash-on-Delivery. Pickup-code mutton pools must be prepaid through the PA.
- Settlement timelines follow the PA–merchant agreement. Refunds route back through escrow.
- Razorpay has applied this rule to Route. Live Route needs GST-3B proof of more than Rs 40L turnover plus approval of a use-case description (routepriority@razorpay.com, 5–7 business days). Pre-existing Route users who missed the 31 Dec 2025 deadline lost Route access.
- The rule comes from RBI, so every Indian PA's split product (Cashfree, PayU, Pine Labs, Juspay) is bound by it.
- Action: check whether the founder's existing Pvt Ltd has GST-3B turnover above Rs 40L and could be the merchant of record. Otherwise the investor demo runs fully in test mode, which is still real APIs, webhooks, holds and refunds, and the live pilot waits on eligibility.
- Also: do not build seller payouts from POOL's own bank account (for example via RazorpayX). That would look like unauthorised payment aggregation.

USA (USD): use Stripe Connect in a sandbox.
- Why not Stripe India: it has been invite-only since May 2024, and India platforms cannot use separate charges and transfers. Live US operation needs a US entity (for example via Stripe Atlas, $500).
- Flow:
  1. Create a PaymentIntent with transfer_group=pool_id. If the pool closes within about 5–7 days, use capture_method=manual so joining places a real card hold.
  2. When the buyer accepts, capture with amount_to_capture set to the accepted price. A partial capture releases the rest automatically.
  3. If the buyer walks away, cancel the PaymentIntent.
  4. On the delivery code, create a Transfer with source_transaction to the dealer's connected account, minus commission.
  5. At pool close, pay Wave Drop as a partial refund.
- Manual payouts can also hold a US connected account's balance for up to 2 years.
- Onboard dealers with the embedded onboarding component. Stripe runs KYC.
- Stripe says plainly that it does not provide escrow. Market this as "held until delivery", not "escrow". The same applies in India, where "escrow" is RBI's term for the PA's own account.

TAX:
- India: GST TCS of 0.5% under s.52 and TDS of 0.1% under s.194-O on dealer payouts (secondary sources only).
- US: marketplace-facilitator sales tax via Stripe Tax.
- US: the 1099-K threshold is back to more than $20k and more than 200 transactions (IRS, OBBB).

LEDGER: keep a double-entry ledger in PostgreSQL from day one, with booking, hold, capture, transfer, rebate and refund entries. TigerBeetle, Formance and Blnk are options for later.

AGENTIC RAILS (ACP, AP2, UCP, Visa Intelligent Commerce, Mastercard Agent Pay, Razorpay/NPCI agentic UPI) are real and active in 2026. They are all beta, pilot, waitlist or region-limited: Stripe's Agentic Commerce Suite covers the US, Canada and Europe only, not India. Show them in the pitch as roadmap, not as the prototype's payment path.

For the prototype you can use right away: the Razorpay MCP server and the Stripe MCP / agent toolkit as developer tools.

items.name: Razorpay Payment Gateway (Orders/Payments: UPI, cards, netbanking, wallets)
items.what_for_in_pool: Booking payment and final accepted-bid payment in INR; webhooks drive pool state
items.reason: Test mode is available immediately after signup with no KYC; the split, hold, refund and MCP ecosystem is the deepest in India.
items.sandbox_or_test: Self-serve test keys (rzp_test_) right after signup; 'No real money is used in the test mode'
items.cost_notes: Standard 2% per successful domestic txn incl. UPI/RuPay, no setup/AMC, +18% GST on fees (pricing page)
items.prerequisites: Live: KYC of POOL's legal entity, website/T&C/refund policy
items.limits_risks: Test and live entities are separate; live activation is a KYC review
items.activity_2026: Active (SDK and MCP repos pushed Aug/Sep 2026)

items.name: Razorpay Route (Linked Accounts + transfers on_hold / modify hold / reversals)
items.category: India split settlement + hold until delivery
items.what_for_in_pool: Transfer the dealer share with on_hold=true at order creation; release on delivery/pickup code via PATCH /v1/transfers/:id {on_hold:false}; keep POOL commission; reverse on disputes
items.reason: The only verified Indian API with an indefinite per-transfer hold (on_hold_until optional), release by PATCH, partial reversals and linked-account KYC via API. It maps exactly to 'money held until code'.
items.sandbox_or_test: Linked accounts and transfers are testable in test mode (FAQ: penny testing in test and live; transfers via orders are API-only). Whether Route is on by default in test mode is not stated; confirm with support.
items.cost_notes: Pricing page: Route 0.1% + platform fees per txn; FAQ: PG fee on the full amount plus a transfer fee on each linked-account transfer, +GST
items.prerequisites: LIVE GATE (RBI PA MD 15-Sep-2025): POOL must show domestic turnover > Rs 40L (GST-3B) or export > Rs 5L for FY25/FY26, plus a payer-payee transparency use-case approved by Razorpay (routepriority@razorpay.com, 5-7 business days). Linked account needs PAN/GSTIN, stakeholder, product configuration, bank account.
items.limits_risks: INR only; no transfers on orders with partial_payment; 24h cooling period after linked-account creation; linked-account settlement takes 2 working days; VPA transfers max Rs 1L; a linked account is either VPA or bank, not both

items.name: Razorpay Refunds API (full / partial / multiple partial, speed=optimum) + Route reverse_all
items.category: India refunds (booking refund, walk-away, Wave Drop rebate)
items.what_for_in_pool: Refund the booking when a buyer walks away; pay Wave Drop rebates at pool close as partial refunds; recover the dealer share with reverse_all or transfer reversals
items.reason: Partial and multiple partial refunds are verified up to the captured amount; receipt works as an idempotency key; the optimum speed gives instant refunds.
items.sandbox_or_test: Works with test keys
items.cost_notes: Instant refund fee Rs 7.99 (up to Rs 1k) / 11.99 (1k-25k) / 14.99 (>25k); normal refunds take 5-7 working days
items.limits_risks: Normal refunds not possible after 6 months; instant refunds not supported on EMI, Cardless EMI and Pay Later; reverse_all cannot be used for partial refunds when the payment was split across multiple linked accounts (use the transfer reversal API)

items.name: Razorpay EMI (credit/debit card EMI, cardless EMI, no-cost/low-cost EMI)
items.what_for_in_pool: Let buyers pay the accepted appliance price in EMI through POOL checkout
items.reason: Enabled from Dashboard payment-method settings, with test cards and an EMI demo; this is table stakes for Indian appliance buyers.
items.sandbox_or_test: Test cards; demo at razorpay.com/emidemo
items.limits_risks: Cardless EMI and SBI card EMI need approval; no instant refunds on EMI, so Wave Drop refunds on EMI orders go at normal speed; partial-refund behaviour on EMI loans not verified

items.name: Razorpay UPI Reserve Pay (UPI Single-Block-Multi-Debit)
items.what_for_in_pool: Block a booking amount or a small mutton-pool order upfront and debit it on acceptance; also the rail behind agentic UPI
items.reason: Real and live, but capped at Rs 10,000, needs activation through Razorpay support, and supports only some UPI apps.
items.sandbox_or_test: Test-mode availability not documented
items.limits_risks: Max block Rs 10,000; token valid up to 90 days; UPI apps listed: BHIM, INDMoney, Navi, Paytm; bank coverage is partial
items.prerequisites: Support ticket to activate; business category must be eligible for UPI mandates/SBMD

items.name: UPI One-Time Mandate (OTM) via PayU / Pine Labs
items.category: India block-then-capture for the full pool price
items.what_for_in_pool: On 'POOL this', block up to the expected price; on bid acceptance, capture the accepted amount (the rest auto-unblocks); release if the buyer walks away
items.reason: Closest UPI match to 'refundable booking' without a refund round-trip, but compatibility with split/hold settlement and test-mode support are unverified.
items.sandbox_or_test: PayU and Pine Labs docs do not state OTM sandbox details
items.limits_risks: Block up to 60 days; single capture only (full or partial); Pine Labs FAQ: up to Rs 1 lakh per mandate for general merchants; the customer cannot revoke from a third-party app

items.name: Razorpay Magic Checkout
items.what_for_in_pool: Saved addresses and one-click checkout for repeat pool buyers
items.reason: On-demand activation, built around COD and e-commerce carts; compatibility with Route/marketplace is not documented. Not needed for the pitch.
items.limits_risks: India only; its COD features conflict with the PA-escrow no-COD rule for marketplace settlement

items.limits_risks: Use test keys only; never give agents live keys with refund/capture rights

items.what_for_in_pool: Node/TypeScript backend calls for orders, payments, Route transfers, refunds and webhooks

items.name: Cashfree Payments PG + Easy Split
items.what_for_in_pool: Backup for Route: vendor (dealer) onboarding, order-level splits, deferred and on-demand vendor settlement, split-aware refunds
items.reason: A solid second PA (RBI-authorised PA, CoA 266/2025), but deferred settlement is capped at 45 days, after which funds auto-release to vendors. That is riskier than Route's indefinite hold for delayed deliveries.
items.sandbox_or_test: Sandbox documented; the FAQ says Easy Split must be activated for both Test and Production; vendor activation takes about 10 minutes in sandbox
items.cost_notes: Easy Split intro 0.2%-0.25% of order value per txn (product page); PG pricing via account manager
items.prerequisites: The same RBI Rs 40L third-party-settlement rule applies (it is an RBI rule, not vendor policy)
items.limits_risks: 45-day max deferral; refunds are deducted from the next vendor settlement
items.license: Proprietary API; Node SDK cashfree-pg 6.0.6 (2026-09-11) Apache-2.0

items.name: Cashfree Secure ID (GSTIN, PAN, PAN-to-GSTIN, bank account / penny-drop verification)
items.what_for_in_pool: Verify dealer GSTIN/PAN and bank account before the 'Verified seller' badge and before creating Route linked accounts
items.reason: Real verification in sandbox, with the environment set by credentials; complements the PA's own KYC with POOL's own seller vetting.
items.sandbox_or_test: Sandbox endpoints e.g. https://sandbox.cashfree.com/verification/gstin
items.prerequisites: Cashfree merchant account; seller consent for data checks

items.name: PayU Split Settlements + Release Settlement API
items.category: India split settlement with explicit release (backup)
items.what_for_in_pool: Split at or after the transaction; call release_settlement per child merchant only after delivery/dispatch
items.reason: Explicit delivery-gated release fits POOL well; keep as the second backup. Older hash-based API style, and only the parent merchant can refund.
items.sandbox_or_test: Test base https://test.payu.in/merchant/ ; the same test cards as web checkout
items.prerequisites: Split feature enablement; RBI Rs 40L third-party-settlement rule applies
items.limits_risks: Refunds only by the parent merchant; max hold before auto-release not documented

items.name: Pine Labs Online (Split Settlements + Release Settlement API; UPI OTM; POS EMI)
items.what_for_in_pool: Held split settlement released by API; UPI OTM; Pine Labs POS EMI when a buyer collects in-store at a dealer
items.reason: The release API is verified (PATCH /api/pay/v1/orders/{orderId}/settlementId/{settlementId}/release), but activation goes through pgsupport@pinelabs.com. Useful when dealers already run Pine Labs POS.
items.sandbox_or_test: UAT base https://pluraluat.v2.pinepg.in
items.prerequisites: Feature activation by Pine Labs; RBI Rs 40L rule

items.name: PhonePe PG Split Settlements
items.what_for_in_pool: Instant split of UPI payments between POOL and vendors
items.reason: PhonePe's page says vendor shares settle immediately on payment confirmation, and no hold/release-on-delivery is documented, which breaks 'money held until code'. The plain PG (UAT sandbox, Node SDK, refunds) is fine as a future extra rail.
items.sandbox_or_test: UAT sandbox exists for PG (developer.phonepe.com)

items.name: Juspay HyperCheckout + Split Settlements
items.what_for_in_pool: Single checkout routing across Razorpay/PayU/Cashfree/Paytm etc., with split settlement passed through to the underlying PA
items.reason: Enterprise and sales-led; split works only where the underlying PA supports it and has onboarded the sub-accounts. Adds cost and complexity before product-market fit.
items.prerequisites: Commercial contract; sub-accounts onboarded at each PA

items.name: juspay/hyperswitch (open-source payment orchestrator)
items.what_for_in_pool: Future single API over Razorpay (India) and Stripe (US) with routing and reconciliation
items.reason: Apache-2.0 and very active. Its Razorpay connector is LIVE (cards, UPI collect, netbanking, refunds), but its docs list split settlement only for Stripe, Adyen and Xendit, NOT Razorpay Route. Self-hosting a Rust stack is overhead a 5-dev team does not need for the prototype.
items.activity_2026: 45.2k stars, Rust, latest release v1.127.0 on 2026-09-28, pushed 2026-09-29
items.sandbox_or_test: Hosted sandbox plus Docker one-click local setup
items.limits_risks: No Razorpay Route split, so POOL's India hold/release would still need direct Route calls

items.name: juspay/hyperswitch-prism (stateless connector library)
items.what_for_in_pool: Lightweight unified request schema across PSPs from Node/TS without running full Hyperswitch
items.reason: Apache-2.0 with Node/TS bindings, but Razorpay coverage and split flows are unverified. Write a thin in-house PaymentProvider interface first.

items.name: RazorpayX Payouts (current account payouts)
items.what_for_in_pool: Paying dealers from POOL's own account (NOT recommended)
items.reason: Collecting buyer money into POOL's own account and paying dealers out is the aggregation activity the RBI PA Directions reserve for authorised PAs; route dealer money through the PA split (Route) instead. Fine later for POOL's own vendor/staff payouts.
items.limits_risks: Regulatory: unauthorised payment aggregation risk; also muddles GST TCS accounting

items.name: ClearTax GST / e-Invoicing GSP APIs
items.what_for_in_pool: GST invoices for POOL commission, GSTR-8 (TCS) filing support, e-invoice IRN when thresholds apply
items.reason: Not needed to demo; needed when live. As an e-commerce operator POOL owes GST TCS (0.5% under s.52) and TDS (0.1% under s.194-O) on dealer payouts; rates come from secondary sources, so confirm with a CA.
items.sandbox_or_test: E-invoice sandbox accepts only specific sandbox GSTINs; sandbox auth token valid 1 hour

items.name: Stripe India (Connect)
items.what_for_in_pool: Would have allowed one PSP for both markets
items.reason: Invite-only since May 2024. For India platforms, separate charges and transfers and standalone transfers are not supported, and manual payouts only for limited cases. It cannot do POOL's hold-then-transfer flow.

items.name: Stripe Connect: separate charges & transfers (transfer_group + source_transaction)
items.category: US split + hold until delivery code
items.what_for_in_pool: Charge the buyer on the POOL platform (transfer_group=pool_id); on delivery/pickup code, create a Transfer to the dealer's connected account with source_transaction, minus commission; reverse transfers on refunds/disputes
items.reason: Verified for US platforms; decouples charge from payout so funds stay on the platform until the code is confirmed; partial transfer reversals supported.
items.sandbox_or_test: Stripe sandboxes / test mode; Connect test data (SSN 000000000, routing 110000000 / account 000123456789)
items.prerequisites: Live: a US legal entity with EIN and US bank account; Stripe platform review
items.limits_risks: Stripe: 'doesn't provide escrow' (do not market as escrow); refunds and chargebacks debit the platform balance; for async methods (ACH) wait for charge.succeeded; 'funds segregation' holding state is private preview only; platform and connected accounts must be in supported regions (US listed, India not)

items.name: Stripe manual capture (authorisation hold) + partial capture
items.category: US refundable booking / hold at join
items.what_for_in_pool: Authorise the buyer's card when they tap 'POOL this'; capture only the accepted price with amount_to_capture (the remainder auto-releases); cancel the PaymentIntent if they walk away, with no refund fee
items.reason: A real hold with no money moved, and cheaper than refunding. Ideal when pools close within the auth window.
items.sandbox_or_test: Test cards 4242... etc.
items.limits_risks: Online CIT auth window 7 days (Visa MIT 5); extended auth up to 30 days only on IC+ pricing or via support, +0.08% on Visa for non-travel categories; only one capture on most payments; also supported for Affirm (30d), Klarna (28d), Afterpay (13d), Cash App Pay (7d), PayPal (up to 20d)

items.name: Stripe Refunds (partial, multiple partial)
items.what_for_in_pool: Wave Drop rebate at pool close as partial refunds; walk-away refunds after capture
items.reason: Multiple partial refunds are supported up to the charge amount, with refund.* webhooks.
items.limits_risks: Stripe processing fees on the original charge are not returned, so rebates cost POOL fees; refunds go only to the original payment method; 5-10 business days to appear; on SCT, refunds debit the platform and you must reverse transfers yourself

items.name: Stripe Connect manual payouts / delay_days (Balance Settings API)
items.what_for_in_pool: Keep dealer balances unpaid until returns or installation windows close; trigger payouts via the Payouts API
items.reason: US connected accounts can hold funds up to 2 years under manual payouts (90 days in most other countries); useful for returns windows.
items.limits_risks: Must pay out within the country limit; Stripe says to use this for delivery delays or refund risk, not as escrow

items.name: Stripe Connect embedded onboarding + Accounts v2 (dealer KYC)
items.what_for_in_pool: Dealers complete Stripe-run KYC (identity, business, bank) inside POOL's dealer portal; the 'recipient' configuration enables receiving transfers
items.reason: Real KYC with test-data outcomes. Themeable, localized, handles documents and bank accounts. No need to build KYC.
items.sandbox_or_test: Test identity values (SSN 000000000 match, 111111111 mismatch; address_full_match); trigger cards to test requirement changes
items.limits_risks: controller.stripe_dashboard.type is immutable; Accounts v2 cannot yet be used with a recipient service agreement, OAuth, or some capabilities (use v1 there); Express/Custom (legacy) makes the platform liable for negative balances

items.name: stripe-node + @stripe/stripe-js (+ stripe-react-native)
items.what_for_in_pool: Server PaymentIntents, Transfers, Refunds and webhooks; client Payment Element; mobile app
items.reason: Official, MIT, TypeScript-first, very active.
items.activity_2026: npm stripe 22.6.2 (2026-09-09), 4.5k stars, pushed 2026-09-29; @stripe/stripe-js 9.17.0 (2026-09-21); stripe-react-native 1.4k stars pushed 2026-09-28

items.name: Stripe CLI + sandboxes
items.what_for_in_pool: Forward webhooks to localhost, trigger events, tail logs; separate sandboxes for dev, CI and the investor-demo environment
items.reason: Apache-2.0, official. `stripe sandbox create` gives working test keys without registration.
items.sandbox_or_test: Anonymous CLI sandboxes expire after 7 days (claimable), so for the investor demo use a registered account's sandbox; a platform sandbox cannot be linked to separate connected-account sandboxes (create connected accounts inside the platform sandbox)

items.name: Stripe Tax
items.what_for_in_pool: Compute sales tax so the US 'guaranteed all-in price' is truly all-in; marketplace-facilitator collection; later registration and filing
items.reason: Works with PaymentIntents and Connect; test-mode calculations make the US demo honest about tax.
items.cost_notes: API integration US$0.50 per transaction where registered (10 calc calls included, 5c each extra); no-code 0.5%; US filing powered by TaxJar
items.limits_risks: POOL must decide marketplace-facilitator obligations per state with a US tax advisor

items.name: Stripe Connect 1099 tax reporting
items.what_for_in_pool: File and deliver 1099-K for dealers when POOL controls pricing (platform pays fees)
items.reason: Needed only at live scale. Stripe files 1099-K itself only where the connected account pays fees; under POOL's model the platform is responsible.
items.limits_risks: 1099-K threshold: > $20,000 AND > 200 transactions (IRS, One Big Beautiful Bill)

items.name: Stripe Atlas (Delaware C-corp / LLC)
items.category: US entity for live US payments
items.what_for_in_pool: Create the US entity (EIN, bank, Stripe US account) needed to go live in the US and to raise from US investors
items.reason: Not needed for the sandbox demo, but Stripe India cannot run the US flow, so any live US pilot requires a US entity. Start early.
items.cost_notes: $500 one-time (includes first year of registered agent), $100/yr after; $2,500 Stripe credits
items.limits_risks: Cross-border structure (India Pvt Ltd plus US entity) needs CA/lawyer advice (FEMA/ODI) — not verified here

items.name: Adyen for Platforms (Marketplaces)
items.what_for_in_pool: Alternative to Stripe Connect: balance accounts, splits, hold funds, hosted onboarding
items.reason: Capable (split at authorisation, custom payout timing, hosted KYC) but sales-led and enterprise-oriented; India is not a supported region.
items.limits_risks: Supported regions: US, CA, Europe/EEA, UK, AU, HK, NZ, SG; test-account signup process for platforms not verified

items.name: Braintree Marketplace (PayPal)
items.what_for_in_pool: Escrow-style hold and release to US sub-merchants
items.reason: Docs say new merchants must contact Sales rather than integrate; US-domiciled master and sub-merchants only; incompatible with PayPal and recurring billing.

items.name: Escrow.com API
items.what_for_in_pool: Licensed escrow with inspection-based release, for very high-ticket items only
items.reason: Buyer and seller need Escrow.com accounts and verification, which adds heavy friction for Rs 30k-1L / $500-2k appliance pools. Stripe SCT plus a delivery code covers the need.
items.sandbox_or_test: Sandbox base https://api.escrow-sandbox.com/2017-09-01/ (separate sandbox account)

items.what_for_in_pool: Only if POOL moves ACH outside Stripe or needs extra buyer identity checks
items.reason: Stripe Connect onboarding already verifies dealer banks and identity; Plaid is redundant for the prototype.
items.sandbox_or_test: Free sandbox via Plaid Dashboard signup

items.reason: Apache-2.0 and active, but a smaller community; evaluate alongside Formance/TigerBeetle post-prototype.

res.summary:
PLATFORM-OSS LENS: what we build on and what we build ourselves. All repo facts below were checked live against the GitHub API (gh api) on 2026-09-29: licence file, stars, last push and latest release. Docs facts were checked on the official sites.

1) CORE FINDING: there is no production-grade open-source "pool + sealed bid + guaranteed price" engine to reuse. A GitHub search for "reverse auction", "sealed bid auction" and "group buying" returns only guides, toy apps, blockchain contracts and one 18-star Rust OTC RFQ engine. So the POOL engine is our own IP: pools, the booking deposit, sealed bids, accept/walk-away, Wave Drop slabs and handover codes. We build it as custom modules on a proven TypeScript commerce/marketplace core. ERPNext's request_for_quotation and supplier_quotation doctypes are domain reference only.

2) RECOMMENDED CORE:
- Medusa v2 (v2.21.2, 28 Sep 2026, MIT) plus Mercur (v2.3.5, MIT). Mercur is a multi-vendor layer on Medusa 2.21. It gives us:
  - seller onboarding
  - an Offer module, where many sellers list offers against one master product (the closest primitive to dealer bids)
  - rule-based commissions
  - per-seller order splitting
  - a pluggable IPayoutProvider (Stripe Connect is built in)
  - admin and vendor panels, and a Next.js storefront
- Critical constraint: Mercur's payout module talks to exactly ONE provider per deployment. That fits a two-region design: an India stack (Razorpay-Route-type custom payout provider + custom Medusa payment provider, INR) and a US stack (Stripe, USD), running the same codebase. The India stack's payment data then stays in India, as RBI requires.
- Do NOT enable Medusa RBAC or SSO. Those files are under a proprietary ENTERPRISE-LICENSE, and switching the flag on counts as claiming you hold a commercial licence.
- Medusa scheduled jobs are cron-only, so they cannot run per-pool timers.
- Medusa ships only a Stripe payment provider. There is a community Razorpay plugin, but it has 17 stars and we found no evidence it supports split payments.

3) TIMERS: Temporal Cloud (MIT SDK) for pool close, bid window, accept window, holding payout until the delivery code is entered, and Wave Drop partial refunds at close.
- Regions include AWS Mumbai (ap-south-1), Hyderabad (ap-south-2) and US.
- Timers survive restarts; sleep() and condition() can wait for months.
- Pricing: $50 per million actions, plus $150 of credits for 90 days.
- Trigger.dev (Apache-2.0) is the lighter alternative. Inngest's server is under SSPL.

4) DATA:
- PostgreSQL 18.6 (19 is only at Beta 4), plus PostGIS for dealer radius and pgvector for matching products (AI suggests, never invents).
- Valkey 9 (BSD) instead of Redis 8, which is now tri-licensed RSAL/SSPL/AGPL.
- BullMQ for jobs, Meilisearch for search.
- Drizzle for services outside Medusa. Avoid Prisma for now: npm "latest" points to 8.0.0-rc.

5) SUPPORTING PIECES:
- Novu (MIT core) for notifications: WhatsApp Business via the Cloud API schema, Gupshup/Twilio/Plivo SMS, in-app inbox.
- Chatwoot (MIT core) for the support desk: the source has WhatsApp Cloud and 360dialog providers.
- Better Auth (phone-number and organization plugins) or Medusa auth with a custom phone OTP.
- Socket.IO for live pool counters. Sealed bids are never broadcast.
- Front end: Next.js 16, shadcn/ui, next-intl, MapLibre.
- Link extraction: Vercel AI SDK with Zod structured output, plus Playwright, Crawlee and metascraper. For Amazon and Flipkart links, check each site's rules; official affiliate/product APIs are covered in the connectors lens.
- Sentry and OpenTelemetry for errors and tracing; PostHog Cloud for analytics and feature flags.
- Ledger: Postgres double-entry tables for now. TigerBeetle later; its two-phase pending, partial-post and void transfers map exactly to the booking hold and Wave Drop.

6) LICENCE FLAGS:
- Strong copyleft (AGPL-3.0): Metabase, Grafana, Plausible, ToolJet, Twenty, Documenso, Unleash (it changed from Apache to AGPL).
- MinIO's repo is ARCHIVED and no longer maintained (it points to the commercial AIStor), so avoid it and use S3.
- Other restrictive licences: Sentry server is FSL; n8n uses the Sustainable Use Licence (not open source); Inngest's server is SSPL; Vendure is GPLv3 or commercial.
- Open core (MIT outside enterprise folders): PostHog, Chatwoot, Novu, SigNoz, GrowthBook, Mastra (Apache outside ee/). Meilisearch is MIT plus BUSL for its enterprise parts.

7) REGULATION:
- RBI circular DPSS.CO.OD.No 2785/06.08.005/2017-18 (6 Apr 2018): payment system data (customer, payment-sensitive, credential and transaction data) must be stored only in India. It can be processed abroad but must be deleted there within 24 hours or one business day. So run the India stack on AWS ap-south-1, pin Vercel functions to bom1, and do not send transaction PII to Sentry (US/EU only), PostHog (US/EU only) or Clerk (US only, no region choice).
- RBI Payment Aggregator Directions 2025 (RBI/DPSS/2025-26/141, 15 Sep 2025): a PA business "shall not carry out marketplace business", and PA funds sit in escrow at a scheduled commercial bank. So POOL must never hold buyer money itself. Hold, split and release must happen inside an authorised PA's escrow and linked-account setup.

8) COMMERCE ENGINES REJECTED FOR A TypeScript TEAM:
- Spree 5 (BSD-3, Ruby): now has marketplace, payouts and a seller panel in the open-source core. It is the strongest non-TS alternative.
- Saleor (Python, no multi-vendor module in its README).
- Vendure (GPLv3; its multi-vendor support is only an example plugin).
- Sylius, Bagisto and Shopware (PHP).

items.name: Medusa v2 (medusajs/medusa)

Built-in providers verified in source: payment-stripe, file-s3, notification-sendgrid, analytics-posthog, auth-emailpass/google/github/oidc, workflow-engine-redis, locking-postgres/redis, search-postgres, translation module.

items.name: Amazon S3 (ap-south-1 + us-east-1)
items.what_for_in_pool: Product images, dealer KYC documents, invoices, delivery proof photos; Medusa file-s3 provider built in.
items.reason: Managed, regional buckets satisfy India localisation for KYC/transaction docs.
items.limits_risks: Keep India buckets in ap-south-1; block cross-region replication of India payment data.

items.name: MinIO (minio/minio)
items.what_for_in_pool: Self-hosted S3.
items.activity_2026: Repository ARCHIVED; README: 'THIS REPOSITORY IS NO LONGER MAINTAINED' (points to AIStor); last release 2025-10-15
items.reason: Unmaintained community edition + AGPL.

items.name: RustFS (rustfs/rustfs)
items.what_for_in_pool: Apache-licensed S3-compatible storage if self-hosting ever needed.
items.reason: Just reached 1.0; S3 is simpler.

items.name: SeaweedFS (seaweedfs/seaweedfs)
items.what_for_in_pool: Self-hosted S3-compatible blob store.
items.reason: Only if leaving managed S3.

items.name: Socket.IO (socketio/socket.io)
items.what_for_in_pool: Live pool state: buyers joined, time to close, number of sealed bids received (never amounts), bid-accepted events to dealer panel.
items.reason: Simplest proven realtime for Node; Valkey adapter for multi-instance.

items.name: Centrifugo (centrifugal/centrifugo)
items.what_for_in_pool: Scalable realtime fan-out server.
items.reason: Needed only at high concurrency.

items.name: Next.js (vercel/next.js)
items.what_for_in_pool: Buyer web/PWA (paste link, pool page, checkout), landing pages, SSR for shareable pool links (WhatsApp previews).
items.reason: Team standard; note Mercur storefront currently on Next 15.5.

items.name: shadcn/ui (shadcn-ui/ui)
items.what_for_in_pool: Accessible component system for buyer, dealer and ops UIs.
items.reason: Copy-in components, no lock-in.

items.name: next-intl (amannn/next-intl)
items.what_for_in_pool: en-IN / hi / te / en-US UI strings; INR and USD formatting via Intl; per-locale routing.
items.reason: Native App Router i18n.

items.name: i18next (i18next/i18next)
items.what_for_in_pool: Shared translations for future Expo apps/back-end messages.
items.reason: Needed when native apps arrive.

items.name: Zod + React Hook Form + TanStack Query
items.what_for_in_pool: Zod: one schema for API validation AND LLM structured output (product identity); RHF: bid/checkout forms; TanStack Query: data fetching/caching.
items.activity_2026: Zod v4.6.5 (2026-09-13); react-hook-form v7.89.0 (2026-09-26); TanStack Query release 2026-09-26
items.reason: Standard, stable TS toolkit.

items.name: Expo / React Native (expo/expo)
items.what_for_in_pool: Native buyer and dealer apps (push alerts for new pools, pickup-code scanner).
items.activity_2026: expo 57.0.26 and react-native 0.87.1 on npm; last push 2026-09-29; ~52.5k stars
items.reason: Ship responsive web/PWA + WhatsApp first; native after prototype.

items.name: MapLibre GL JS (maplibre/maplibre-gl-js)
items.what_for_in_pool: Dealer location/pickup map, delivery radius display.
items.reason: No per-load fees; pair with a tile source.

items.name: PMTiles / Protomaps (protomaps/PMTiles)
items.what_for_in_pool: Single-file basemap tiles served from S3 for MapLibre.
items.license: BSD-3 reference implementations; spec public domain/CC0; sample tilesets own terms
items.reason: Use a hosted tile provider for prototype; self-host tiles later.

items.name: Vercel AI SDK (vercel/ai)
items.what_for_in_pool: Provider-agnostic LLM calls with Zod-typed structured output for product identification from extracted page data; tool calling; streaming.
items.reason: Swap models per region/cost without rewriting; schema-constrained outputs reduce hallucination.
items.limits_risks: Model choice/pricing is covered by the models lens.

items.name: Mastra (mastra-ai/mastra)
items.what_for_in_pool: TS agent framework (e.g., dealer-assist agent drafting bids).
items.license: Apache-2.0 outside ee/ directories (ee under separate licence)
items.reason: Not needed for deterministic extraction.

items.name: LangGraph.js (langchain-ai/langgraphjs)
items.what_for_in_pool: Agent graphs.
items.reason: Overlaps AI SDK.

items.name: Playwright (microsoft/playwright)
items.what_for_in_pool: Headless rendering of JS-heavy brand/retailer product pages to read title, model number, price, schema.org data; also E2E tests of pool flow.
items.reason: Real extraction, not mocked.
items.limits_risks: Respect site ToS/robots; marketplace sites (Amazon/Flipkart) restrict scraping — prefer their official product/affiliate APIs (connectors lens).

items.name: Crawlee (apify/crawlee)
items.what_for_in_pool: Request queue, retries, session/proxy rotation, Playwright/Cheerio crawlers for link resolution.
items.reason: Production-grade crawling primitives in TS.

items.name: metascraper (microlinkhq/metascraper)
items.what_for_in_pool: Fast first pass: Open Graph / JSON-LD / microdata metadata from pasted URLs before invoking browser or LLM.
items.reason: Cheap deterministic extraction reduces LLM calls.

items.name: Mozilla Readability (mozilla/readability)
items.what_for_in_pool: Clean page text before LLM parsing.
items.reason: Product pages are better parsed via structured data.

items.name: razorpay-node (official SDK)
items.what_for_in_pool: India stack: orders, payments, refunds (incl. partial), Route/transfers for dealer split — used inside the custom Medusa payment provider and Mercur IPayoutProvider.
items.reason: Official SDK; feature/endpoint verification is in the payments/connectors lens.
items.prerequisites: Razorpay account; Route/linked accounts need KYC activation.

items.name: stripe-node (official SDK)
items.what_for_in_pool: US stack: PaymentIntents, refunds, Connect transfers/payouts (Mercur Stripe Connect payout provider).
items.reason: Medusa payment-stripe + Mercur payout-stripe-connect already built on Stripe.
items.sandbox_or_test: Self-serve test mode keys.

items.name: SGFGOV medusa-payment-plugins (medusa-plugin-razorpay-v2)
items.what_for_in_pool: Reference code for a Medusa v2 Razorpay payment provider (UPI, cards, netbanking, wallets, INR).
items.reason: Low adoption and no evidence of Route split support; write our own provider using it as reference.

items.name: Hyperswitch (juspay/hyperswitch)
items.what_for_in_pool: Multi-PSP routing/failover/vault; connectors in source include razorpay, stripe, phonepe, paytm, payu, adyen, checkout, braintree.
items.reason: Adds a Rust service + vault; integrate Razorpay/Stripe directly for prototype, add routing at scale.

items.name: TigerBeetle (tigerbeetle/tigerbeetle)
items.what_for_in_pool: Double-entry ledger with two-phase transfers: pending (booking deposit hold), post_pending with partial amount (remainder restored = Wave Drop), void_pending (walk-away refund), timeout expiry; Node client.
items.reason: Perfect semantic fit but extra infra; prototype mirrors PA state in Postgres ledger tables (real money stays in PA escrow).

items.name: Formance Ledger (formancehq/ledger)
items.what_for_in_pool: Programmable ledger alternative.
items.reason: Evaluate alongside TigerBeetle post-prototype.

items.name: Blnk (blnkfinance/blnk)
items.what_for_in_pool: Ledger with inflight transactions.
items.reason: Young/small community.

items.name: NestJS / Hono
items.what_for_in_pool: Standalone services outside Medusa (link-extraction API, webhook ingress) if needed.
items.reason: Medusa API routes cover prototype; add only if services split out.

items.name: n8n (n8n-io/n8n)
items.what_for_in_pool: Internal ops automations (dealer onboarding reminders, reports).
items.license: Sustainable Use License (fair-code, not OSI) + .ee files under enterprise licence
items.reason: Internal use only; cannot be embedded/offered as a service to dealers.

items.name: Twenty CRM (twentyhq/twenty)
items.what_for_in_pool: Dealer acquisition pipeline for ops team.
items.license: AGPL-3.0 with some commercial-licensed files and some MIT packages
items.reason: AGPL; a spreadsheet/Appsmith suffices for 4 ops.

items.name: Documenso (documenso/documenso)
items.what_for_in_pool: Dealer agreement e-signing.
items.reason: AGPL; not needed for prototype.

items.name: Coolify (coollabsio/coolify)
items.what_for_in_pool: Self-hosted PaaS on own VMs.
items.reason: Managed AWS/Vercel faster for 5 devs.

items.name: AWS ap-south-1 (Mumbai) + us-east-1 (N. Virginia)
items.what_for_in_pool: Two regional stacks of one codebase: India (Medusa/Mercur, Postgres, Valkey, Novu, Chatwoot, Metabase, S3) in ap-south-1; US in us-east-1.
items.reason: Both enabled by default; Mumbai satisfies RBI payment-data localisation; same services both sides.
items.limits_risks: Never replicate India payment/transaction data to the US region.

items.name: AWS ap-south-2 (Hyderabad)
items.what_for_in_pool: Second India region for DR/backups within India.
items.reason: Opt-in region (disabled by default); useful for in-country DR; Temporal Cloud also offers aws-ap-south-2.

items.name: Vercel (bom1 Mumbai + iad1 Washington DC)
items.what_for_in_pool: Host Next.js buyer/dealer frontends per region.
items.reason: 19 compute regions incl. bom1 (ap-south-1) and iad1; fastest deploys.
items.limits_risks: Functions default to iad1 — pin India project functions to bom1 so payment/PII requests are processed in India; keep payment logic in AWS backend.

items.name: RBI Storage of Payment System Data (DPSS.CO.OD.No 2785/06.08.005/2017-18, 6 Apr 2018)
items.what_for_in_pool: Architecture constraint: customer data, payment-sensitive data, credentials and transaction data for payment systems stored only in India; processing abroad allowed but must be deleted abroad and brought back within one business day or 24 hours; cross-border transactions may keep foreign-component copy abroad.
items.reason: Directly binds PSOs/PAs and flows through intermediaries; design India stack in-country now to pass PA/partner due diligence.
items.limits_risks: Applies to authorised system providers; POOL inherits via PA contracts — keep US SaaS (Sentry/PostHog/Clerk) free of Indian transaction data.

items.name: RBI (Regulation of Payment Aggregators) Directions, 2025 (RBI/DPSS/2025-26/141, 15 Sep 2025)
items.what_for_in_pool: Money-flow constraint: 'A PA business shall not carry out marketplace business'; non-bank PA funds held in escrow with a scheduled commercial bank; settlement timelines per PA-merchant agreement; PA does merchant due diligence (CKYCR, simplified for < Rs 40 lakh turnover).
items.reason: POOL must not collect/hold buyer funds itself; booking hold, split and delayed release must happen inside an authorised PA's escrow/linked-account product.
items.limits_risks: Get counsel sign-off on POOL's exact flow (booking deposit, hold until code, partial refunds) before live money.
